validity.recommendation: keep as operating; existence, classification, ownership structure and route are all well documented and non-duplicate
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE CONFIRMED, independent of GEM/wiki, across an 18-year documentary record (Dec 2006 announcement through FY2025 SEC filings filed Feb 2026). Kinder Morgan and Energy Transfer Partners announced the 50/50 joint venture in December 2006 (KMP's own Jan 17, 2007 8-K exhibit press release); the entity Midcontinent Express Pipeline LLC was formed and initiated FERC NEPA pre-filing review by Feb 2007 (ETP's FY2008 10-K exhibit); FERC issued the CP08-6 certificate in June 2008; the pipeline entered interim service April 10, 2009, achieved full Zone 1/Zone 2 service by August 1, 2009 (SEC EDGAR dex993.htm, MEP LLC's own audited 2010 financial statements); and it remains an active, revenue-generating, 50%-Kinder-Morgan-owned asset in both co-owners' FY2025 10-Ks (filed Feb 2026). Classification is correct: a FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural gas TRANSMISSION pipeline (Docket CP08-6, NGA Section 7 certificate), confirmed by the Federal Register notice of application and every source found. No duplicate found against the other 44 rows on the US-gas roster -- it is a standalone ~507-515-mile mainline, distinct from (though a sibling 50/50-JV-structure pipeline to) Fayetteville Express Pipeline (P0189, KMI/Energy Transfer JV in Arkansas-to-Mississippi, per the batch's explicit warning not to cross-cite FEP and MEP despite shared owners -- confirmed as genuinely separate systems: MEP runs Bennington OK -> Butler AL, FEP runs Conway County AR -> Panola County MS, and MEP's operator is Kinder Morgan while FEP's operator is Energy Transfer, the reverse assignment). Owner2 'ETP Legacy' is not a real current entity name -- see the attribution concern below.

validity.recommendation: correct Owner2 from 'ETP Legacy' to 'Energy Transfer' -- ETP Legacy is not a current entity name found in any source
validity.researcher_notes: Per the orchestrator's specific instruction to check how Energy Transfer's interest is actually held today: NO source of any kind (SEC filings, press, either co-owner's own materials) uses the string 'ETP Legacy' for this or any other asset. Full ownership-chain history, traced via MEP LLC's own SEC-filed 2010 audited financial statements (dex993.htm): the JV entity was formed March 1, 2007, initially 50.0% owned by Kinder Morgan Operating Limited Partnership 'A' (KMOLPA, a KMP subsidiary) and 50.0% by 'ETC Midcontinent Express Pipeline, L.L.C.' (a wholly-owned subsidiary of Energy Transfer Partners, L.P.). On April 12, 2010, that ETP-side interest was passed down through ETC Midcontinent Express II and III (all then-ETP subsidiaries); on May 26, 2010, ETE transferred the ETC Midcontinent III interest (49.9%) to Regency Energy Partners LP; by June 2010 the ETP-side interest was split 0.1% ETC Midcontinent Express II / 49.9% Regency Midcontinent Express Pipeline I LLC. Regency Energy Partners was itself absorbed into Energy Transfer Partners in 2015, and ETP was in turn absorbed into Energy Transfer LP in 2018 -- so the full chain of 'ETP'-branded intermediate entities has been dissolved/merged away. Energy Transfer LP's own FY2025 10-K Exhibit 21.1 (subsidiary list, filed Feb 2026) confirms 'ETC Midcontinent Express Pipeline, L.L.C.' still exists TODAY as a direct Energy Transfer LP subsidiary, and both co-owners' FY2025 10-Ks independently state the JV remains 50/50 with Kinder Morgan operating the system. Recommend Owner2='Energy Transfer' (matching GEM's own current-company convention, as already used for Owner1 on the sibling P0189 row), Owner2%=50.00% unchanged; 'ETC Midcontinent Express Pipeline, L.L.C.' is the more precise subsidiary name if the sheet wants it.

validity.recommendation: correct Capacity from 1,533.00 MMcf/d (the original 2009 as-built design capacity) to approximately 1,800.00 MMcf/d, reflecting a June 2010 compression expansion that has been the pipeline's current capacity for over 15 years
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's recorded 1,533.00 MMcf/d matches EIA's own project-level entry for MEP's ORIGINAL 'New Pipeline' construction phase (completed 2009-04-10) exactly -- but is now materially stale. THREE independent sources document a subsequent, still-current compression-capacity expansion: (1) MEP LLC's own SEC-filed 2010 audited financial statements (dex993.htm): 'in June 2010, Midcontinent Express completed two natural gas compression projects that increased Zone 1 capacity from 1.5 to 1.8 billion cubic feet per day, and Zone 2 capacity from 1.0 to 1.2 billion cubic feet per day. The incremental capacity is fully subscribed with ten-year binding shipper agreements'; (2) ETP's own FY2008 10-K exhibit, describing a July 2008 open season that expanded the planned main-segment capacity 'from the original planned capacity of 1.5 Bcf/d to a total capacity of 1.8 Bcf/d' (fully subscribed, effectuated via additional compression, subject to FERC approval -- which the SEC 2010 financials confirm was completed); (3) Energy Transfer's own FY2025 10-K (filed Feb 2026): 'Midcontinent Express Pipeline 50% 510 1.8 --' in its current interstate-pipeline asset table. Kinder Morgan's own FY2025 10-K gives a slightly more precise 1.81 Bcf/d (515 miles) for the same current asset -- a small but persistent (also present in both companies' FY2024 10-Ks, per the cross-row lead filed on the sibling P0189 shard) cross-owner rounding/measurement difference, not a live disagreement about the fact of the expansion. Per rule 7, filing the corrected value (1,800.00 MMcf/d, matching the majority/SEC-financial-statement figure) alongside this concern rather than silently keeping the stale pre-expansion number or silently overwriting it. Docket for the 2010 expansion is FERC CP09-56 (EIA lists this as a separate 'Midcontinent Express Pipeline Expansion' project entry, completed 2010-05-31, which is likely why EIA's -- and thus GEM's -- main MEP row never picked up the higher post-expansion capacity).
